chapters.narrativeText: Take a moment with the painting itself. Notice the dark charcoal lines that break through the layers of blue and ochre oil paint: the drawing beneath the sea.

hotspots.title: Charcoal Underlayer
hotspots.description: Macro photograph revealing the charcoal drawing beneath the oil surface.

chapters.narrativeText: "It started with sketches on the beach at Espinho in 2017. I drew the same wave every morning for a month." - Inês Valente

hotspots.title: First Draft Study
hotspots.description: Slide to compare the 2017 beach sketch with the final painting.

chapters.narrativeText: "There was a horizon line. I painted over it because the sea in my memory had no end." - Inês Valente

hotspots.title: Hidden Horizon (Pentimento)
hotspots.description: Infrared capture revealing the painted-over horizon line.

chapters.narrativeText: Curatorial note: Valente's work belongs to a generation of Portuguese artists responding to coastal erosion. The 1970s coastline seen here no longer exists, so the painting becomes an archive of a vanishing landscape.

hotspots.title: Archive Photograph, 1974
hotspots.description: Municipal archive image of the same stretch of coast.

chapters.narrativeText: Lower the tablet. Look at the painting again with your own eyes: what do you see now that you did not see before?
